_comment: Authored reply bodies for the synthetic server. These are NOT recovered game data — they are what
WE choose to send, keyed by the request's Header z5hB3P01 (the getRequestID() token), with an optional
'_default'. Values are the DECRYPTED body; capture_server.py wraps and encrypts them with the
request's EncodeKey. Keys consumed by GameSettingResponse are literal P_GS_* names, not 8-char
tokens — see docs/notes/gamesetting_payload_tree.md (verified: 19 P_GS_* literals in libgame.so).
The gacha rates are ours; so is all of this. Never present it as recovered data.

P_GS_CDN_PATH (and the other *_PATH/_HOST_SERVER values) must be a BARE host with NO scheme: the client prepends the scheme itself (CommonUtils::getResourceUrl 0x1e317d4 = scheme + value + "/"), so "https://host/" becomes "https://https://host//..." and the fetch never leaves the device. Precedent in the binary: PHP_URL() is the literal "v900-lapis.gumi.sg" + "/lapisProd/app". Only P_GS_CDN_PATH is proven so far - docs/notes/resource_download.md (S1.7).

75fYdNxq's F_LOCALIZED_TEXT_MST must DIFFER from the client's PERSISTED value for it to re-fetch: makeMstFileName builds "Ver"+version+"_"+name+".dat" from THIS row (F_MST_VERSION is a different field and does not affect the filename). We advertised 705/268 while serving a patched F_TEXT_GACHA. RETIRED 2026-09-20: the banner now uses the REAL gacha id 1, whose title and description already exist in the SHIPPED table ('Standard Summon' / 'Friend point event going on now! ...'), so we advertise the shipped 704 (manifest) and 267 (F_TEXT_GACHA). Both differ from what the client persisted (705/268), so it re-fetches the shipped files straight from the read-only APK tree. docs/notes/mst_version_source.md

lEHBdOEf + mRPo5n2j: switch 90001838 IS the Terms-of-Use gate (F_DEFINE_MST TNC_SWITCH_ID). LoginScene::procStateLoad (STATE_LOAD 0x1c, libgame 0x2235458) shows the 'Terms of Use have been updated' notice iff !UserSwitchInfo::has(90001838) - that is the whole predicate: no pref, no other field. UserSwitchInfo is session-scoped and NEVER persisted (no save/load call anywhere in the 0x1d8a000 blob), so every returning-user session starts with an empty switch dictionary and re-shows the notice; a new-account run skips it only because CreateUserScene::updateEvent sets the id locally. F_SWITCH_MST row for 90001838 = type 9000 / index 9842 -> a 2461-char container with '2' at position 2460. The client's own UpdateSwitchInfoRequest is sent AFTER that state (STATE_UPDATE_SWITCH 0x24 is entered FROM STATE_LOAD), so its reply cannot gate the same visit - hence the record also goes into lEHBdOEf (GetBackgroundDownloadInfo), the one pre-login reply the client cannot proceed without. docs/notes/tos_update_notice_gate.md

75fYdNxq + out/cdn_overlay: F_DEFINE_MST is version-bumped to 227 (persisted is 226) so the client downloads OUR copy of Ver227_zg5P1AxM.dat, in which TNC_SWITCH_ID is 0 instead of 90001838. Why: LoginScene::procStateLoad gates the 'Terms of Use have been updated' notice on DefineMst::getValue<int>("TNC_SWITCH_ID") >= 1 && !UserSwitchInfo::has(id), and DefineMst is filled from the F_DEFINE_MST MST - which today is the SHIPPED Ver224 (our reply never listed F_DEFINE_MST, and the client only downloads when the advertised version differs). Setting it to 0 makes the condition false unconditionally, so the notice cannot appear at all. The switch-grant route was tried first and DISPROVEN by a run: the reply that fills UserSwitchInfo is the answer to the client's own UpdateSwitchInfoRequest, which it sends from the ACCEPT path - i.e. after the gate - and there is no pre-gate client-side writer of that singleton (docs/notes/switch_gate_parse_path.md). Blast radius of 0: the TNC_SWITCH_ID literal has exactly 3 references and all three read 0 as 'no TNC switch'.
